headline: High-risk capability conflict and cascading-error risk: Plandex can write/execute broadly while Dagster is a non-runnable orchestrator with no direct isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or file I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Plandex output by default. Plandex does use stdin/stdout and project files, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is unusual manual copy/paste or external wiring, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Plandex output into a Dagster config or prompt field, injection becomes possible.
IF an external wrapper connects Plandex stdout to Dagster input, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate terminals and avoid copy-paste between them.
Disable any wrapper that forwards Plandex output into Dagster inputs.
Use a plain-text review step before any Dagster ingestion.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any bridged text channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while Plandex reads/writes a project directory and sends context to model providers. There is no documented shared workspace between them, so leakage is not default. If they are pointed at the same directory, Plandex could expose source code that Dagster itself does not handle.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to access the same project directory, Plandex may transmit shared file contents to external services.
IF Dagster is extended to read sensitive files from that directory, leakage scope expands.
mitigations: Use separate directories for Dagster and Plandex.
Do not place secrets in the Plandex project tree.
Review Plandex file access before running on sensitive repos.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster is non-runnable and has no write or shell capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources itself. Plandex can execute shell commands, modify git state, and write files, and its backend supports shared state across instances. The pair therefore has a one-sided but real conflict surface if Dagster-managed artifacts and Plandex edits target the same repo or plan state.
conditions: IF Plandex instances operate on the same repository or plan state, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF Dagster is used to generate files that Plandex also edits, file-level conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Run only one Plandex instance per repo at a time.
Keep Dagster outputs in a separate staging directory.
Use git branches for Plandex changes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared plan or repo state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator, so if Plandex outputs code or configuration that Dagster later consumes, errors can cascade into downstream pipelines. Dagster has no built-in verification surface in the profile, and Plandex supports review-then-apply with optional auto-apply, so unsafe outputs can propagate unless an operator intervenes. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Plandex-generated code or config is fed into Dagster jobs without review, downstream pipeline failures can propagate.
IF Dagster schedules actions based on Plandex output, incorrect assumptions can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before applying Plandex changes.
Validate generated code/config in a staging Dagster environment.
Keep auto-apply disabled for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add schema and test gates before Dagster ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and touches no data classes, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider API keys. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented here, and the pair does not show PHI or EU PII handling. The main compliance concern is ordinary source-code handling, which is lower risk absent a regulated data class.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into Plandex project files, compliance risk increases.
IF Dagster is configured to orchestrate regulated datasets, residency and retention controls must be checked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plandex project files.
Confirm retention settings for any Plandex cloud usage.
Document data-class boundaries for Dagster workflows.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
